description: An eight-panel composite figure that mixes two modalities acquired on the same fields of a 3Cu (Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.8C–3Cu) lightweight steel strip: grayscale electron micrographs (a–d) and colour-coded electron-probe microanalysis (EPMA) Cu maps (e–h). Caption assignment: (a,e) as cast; (b,f) annealed at 500 °C; (c,g) annealed at 600 °C; (d,h) annealed at 700 °C. Panels (a–d) are SEM-type images, each with a "2 µm" scale bar at lower right. (a) shows one large irregular Cu-rich particle (bright outline, right) plus a smaller one upper left in a smooth matrix; (b) shows similar large elongated outlined particles after 500 °C; (c) shows the large particles largely replaced by chains of fine bright dots; (d) shows many smaller, more numerous particles. The maps (e–h) use a dark-blue→green→yellow→red colour scale (no numeric concentration legend is printed); red is strongest in (e), weaker yellow/orange in (f,g), and absent in (h), which shows only diffuse blue-green Cu. The figure demonstrates that raising annealing temperature from 500 to 700 °C progressively dissolves the large Cu-rich areas while fine Cu-rich particles inside austenite become more numerous.

subfigures.description: Grayscale micrograph of the as-cast 3Cu strip with a 2 µm scale bar; one large irregular Cu-rich particle with a bright outline sits at right, a smaller one at upper left, and fine speckle precipitates are dispersed in the smooth matrix.
Grayscale micrograph after annealing at 500 °C with a 2 µm scale bar; large elongated, irregular outlined particles similar in size to (a) occupy the matrix.
Grayscale micrograph after annealing at 600 °C with a 2 µm scale bar; the large particles are largely gone and replaced by a chain of fine bright dots, with a blocky dark region at left.
Grayscale micrograph after annealing at 700 °C with a 2 µm scale bar; many smaller, more numerous particles with dark interiors are distributed over the field.
EPMA Cu map of the as-cast field (a) rendered in blue-green-yellow-red; contains the most intense red hotspots, spatially coincident with the large Cu-rich particles of (a).
EPMA Cu map after 500 °C annealing (field of b); weaker yellow/orange Cu enrichment around the particle positions and isolated red spots, on a dark blue background.
EPMA Cu map after 600 °C annealing (field of c); diffuse green background with a linear chain of yellow/orange/red Cu-rich spots matching the dot chain seen in (c).
EPMA Cu map after 700 °C annealing (field of d); no strong red hotspots, only diffuse green-blue Cu signal spread over the field.

observations.observation: Panels (a–d) are grayscale electron micrographs, each carrying a '2 µm' scale bar in the lower-right corner.
In (a) (as cast) a single large irregular particle with a bright outline, roughly a few µm across, sits at the right of the field, with a smaller particle at upper left.
In (c) the coarse particles are replaced by chains of fine bright dots, and in (d) many more, smaller particles are present.
Panels (e–h) are colour EPMA maps using a blue→green→yellow→red scale, with red marking the highest Cu signal; no numeric concentration legend or scale bar is printed on the maps.

The red Cu hotspots are most intense in the as-cast map (e) and are spatially coincident with the large particles seen in (a); by (h) (700 °C) no strong red hotspots remain, only diffuse blue-green Cu signal.
The caption assigns (a,e) as cast, (b,f) annealed at 500 °C, (c,g) annealed at 600 °C and (d,h) annealed at 700 °C.
The caption identifies the material as 3Cu strips and states the images are electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) images reproduced with permission from Springer Nature, 2021.
The citing text states that as the annealing temperature increases, the size and number of large Cu-rich areas gradually decrease while the number of small Cu-rich areas in the austenite increases.
The citing text states that 0–3 wt% Cu addition suppresses the formation of intergranular κ-carbides during annealing at 500–700 °C for 3 h.
The citing text identifies the alloy studied in this figure as Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.8C–3Cu.
The (g) map shows a linear chain of yellow/orange Cu-rich spots that matches the chain of fine bright dots visible in the corresponding micrograph (c).

unreadable_items: Panels (e)–(h): no colour-scale legend or numeric Cu concentration values are printed, so Cu content cannot be quantified from the maps
Panels (e)–(h): no scale bar or field-of-view marker is visible on the EPMA maps
